negative_findings.description: Neither the hu-language search on kormany.hu consultation terms combined with 'pénzügyi szolgáltatások' nor the open-consultation listing on egyeztetes.kormany.hu surfaced any currently open banking or payments consultation. The only ongoing item observed on the portal was a road-safety dialogue (deadline 2026-09-09); the recently closed items were asset-recovery, secret-service archives and school-start support.
negative_findings.result_summary: No live HU banking/payments ministry consultation observed at scouting time; this is a point-in-time observation, not evidence that the channel is unused.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's channel must be monitored continuously rather than sampled — comment windows are short (5 working days internally, ~8 days publicly) and a sector draft can open and close between polls.

negative_findings.description: The egyeztetes.kormany.hu consultation portal page carried no visible RSS feed or documented API; the current kormany.hu generation likewise did not expose an RSS index in search results, although the frozen 2010-2014 and 2015-2019 generations both published /rss channel lists including one for the document archive.
negative_findings.result_summary: Machine-readable subscription for HU government consultations is unconfirmed on the current site; polling with diffing is the fallback.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Drives the collection architecture and cost for the whole A3 executive-branch channel, and creates a risk of missing short-window drafts.

negative_findings.description: The ministry-filtered dokumentumtár URL for Nemzetgazdasági Minisztérium draft laws rendered 'Nincs találat' when fetched as static HTML, despite search-engine evidence of ~130 items under that filter with 2026 dates and April 2026 comment deadlines.
negative_findings.result_summary: Treated as a client-side-rendering hypothesis, not as a dead or empty source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collector built on plain HTTP fetching would silently record zero HU ministry drafts — a false-negative failure mode that must be guarded with a non-zero-results assertion.

negative_findings.description: https://kormany.hu/kormanyzat/nemzetgazdasagi-miniszterium returned HTTP 404; only the frozen 2020-2025 generation page for NGM could be reached in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Current-generation NGM ministry landing URL unresolved; recorded as unverified/moved rather than dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Ministry slugs and site generations change with each government cycle, so hardcoded ministry URLs will rot; resolution must go through the Kormányzat index each run.

negative_findings.description: The run scope names both Nemzetgazdasági Minisztérium and Pénzügyminisztérium. Evidence in this pass shows NGM as the current owner of financial/economic legislation and NGM-issued ministerial instructions dated 2024, while older financial-sector decrees carry the historic NGM/PM/NFGM prefixes. No page was found that authoritatively maps the PM to NGM portfolio transfer.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ministry-name lineage (NFGM → NGM → PM → NGM) partially inferred from decree prefixes rather than from a confirmed source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Historical backfill and decree-prefix parsing will mis-attribute drafts unless the ministry lineage is explicitly resolved.

negative_findings.description: English-language searching returned almost nothing on the HU executive branch's own consultation channel; the only substantive English-language route into HU pre-adoption drafts found was the EU TRIS notification database.
negative_findings.result_summary: English is not a viable primary monitoring language for this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms Hungarian-language collection and parsing (including Hungarian PDF extraction) is mandatory infrastructure for A3, not optional.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Drive the dokumentumtár with a headless browser once, capture the XHR/API calls it makes, and build the collector on that underlying endpoint rather than on the rendered HTML.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian law requires the responsible minister to publish a summary of received comments and a list of commenters, but no live example of such a summary page for a financial-sector draft was located in this pass.

Beyond NGM and a glance at the Justice Ministry, other ministries that can originate banking/payments-adjacent rules (Miniszterelnökség, Igazságügyi Minisztérium for civil/consumer-credit law, Belügyminisztérium for AML/data) were not individually scouted.

brief: Hungary's executive-branch pre-legislative channel is highly centralised: essentially every ministry draft bill and its comment deadline passes through kormany.hu — the egyeztetes.kormany.hu consultation portal for open items, the Dokumentumtár 'jogszabálytervezetek' shelf (filterable to Nemzetgazdasági Minisztérium, the owner of financial-sector and payments law) for the full packages, and cdn.kormany.hu for the actual draft texts, indokolás and impact-assessment attachments. The process is statutorily framed by the 2010 Jet. law, decree 301/2010 and government decision 1352/2022, which together mean comment windows are very short — five working days internally, roughly eight days publicly — so this cell requires continuous polling rather than periodic sampling, and no RSS or API was confirmed on the current site. Coverage is only workable in Hungarian; English-language routes are effectively limited to EU TRIS notifications of Hungarian draft technical rules. Redundancy against kormany.hu's JavaScript-rendered filters should come from the independent aggregator torvenyfigyelo.hu, the parliamentary iromány register and the Kormány's half-yearly legislative programme (the earliest forward signal), with Magyar Bankszövetség reporting as an indirect confirmer of what the sector was asked to comment on.
